issues.legal_issue: A widow who succeeds to an unprovided shebaitship as a limited holder may devise the enlarged right by will to an eligible successor.
material_facts: The founder dedicated his property to a deity and appointed his wife as shebait, but did not provide for the subsequent devolution of the shebaitship or restrict her interest in it.
No contrary custom or usage was pleaded.
On the founder’s death, his widow succeeded to the shebaitship as a limited holder; her interest was enlarged under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

The widow’s will appointed the second respondent as shebait, and the Court found that the appointee was not disqualified as a non-Hindu and could perform the duties personally or through a suitable person.
The appellant challenged the High Court’s decision recognizing the testamentary appointment.
issues.conclusion: The widow could transfer the shebaitship by will, and the second respondent acquired the shebaiti right under her will. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Shebaitship combines religious office and property and is heritable property. Where the founder has not provided for the devolution of shebaitship and no contrary custom or usage is shown, it devolves under Hindu law; a widow may succeed as a limited holder. Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 enlarges a Hindu female’s limited interest into an absolute one, enabling her to devise the shebaitship to an eligible person who can perform the duties or arrange for their performance. The Court relied on Angurbala Mullick v. Debabrata Mullick, [1951] 2 S.C.R. 1125, Profulla Choronl Requittee v. Satya Choronl Requittee, [1979] 3 S.C.R. 431, and Ram Rattan v. Bajrang Lal, [1979] 3 S.C.R. 963. The concurring judge also referred to the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937. The Court did not express an opinion on the correctness of K.K. Ganguli v. Panna Banerjee, [1975] 1 S.C.R. 728.

rule.if: civil_appeal_challenged_testamentary_shebaitship and founder_created_endowment and founder_did_not_provide_shebait_succession and no_contrary_custom_or_usage and widow_succeeded_as_limited_holder and widow_interest_became_absolute and will_bequeathed_shebaitship and beneficiary_is_hindu_and_can_perform_or_arrange_duties

predicates.civil_appeal_challenged_testamentary_she: An appellant challenged, in a civil appeal, a decision recognizing a testamentary appointment to shebaitship.
predicates.founder_created_endowment: A founder created a religious endowment and appointed a shebait.
predicates.founder_did_not_provide_shebait_successi: The founder did not provide for the subsequent devolution of the shebaitship.
predicates.no_contrary_custom_or_usage: No party pleaded a custom or usage providing for a different devolution of the shebaitship.
predicates.widow_succeeded_as_limited_holder: The founder’s widow succeeded to the shebaitship as a limited holder.
predicates.widow_interest_became_absolute: The widow’s limited interest in the shebaitship became an absolute interest.
predicates.will_bequeathed_shebaitship: The widow’s will designated a beneficiary to succeed to the shebaitship.
predicates.beneficiary_is_hindu_and_can_perform_or_: The designated beneficiary was not a non-Hindu and could perform the shebait’s duties personally or arrange for a suitable person to perform them.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges a testamentary shebaitship appointment and the founder left succession unprovided, no contrary custom or usage applies, the widow succeeded as a limited holder whose interest became absolute, and her will designated an eligible beneficiary, that beneficiary acquires the shebaitship.
